ei.subject: 영어Ⅰ
ei.title: Be Proud of Who You Are

fullPassage:
주어진 글: The funny thing was whenever anyone asked me to play a song for them, I would be so happy. Although my dream was to record an album, the reality was I probably wouldn't make it.

(A) Then I thought of my grandfather and how he loved playing, practicing his art his entire life, even without fame. I realized the only way to become an old guitarist like him was to keep playing.

(B) Then one day, I looked at the picture of The Old Guitarist on my wall. I suddenly remembered what my grandfather had told me about Picasso: only a tiny fraction of the thousands of artworks he created during his lifetime are recognized by the public.

(C) The happy ending to this story is that after having sent my recordings to countless producers, I finally found one who was eager to work with me. One thing led to another, and I finally signed a record deal.

questions.passage: Researchers performed an experiment <u>ⓐ where</u> students were paired up for five-minute ice breaking conversations. They were then asked to rate how much they liked their partners. Additionally, researchers asked participants if they thought their partners liked <u>ⓑ them</u>. Most participants' estimations of their partners' responses were pessimistic, <u>ⓒ which</u> were opposite to the real responses. It turns out that participants do not make bad impressions but <u>ⓓ make</u> better impressions than they <u>ⓔ thinking</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: 참가자들은 그들이 생각하는 것보다 더 좋은 인상을 준다. ⓔ thinking은 비교 접속사 than 뒤의 절에서 주어 they의 동사 역할을 하므로, 현재분사 thinking이 아닌 동사 원형(현재 시제) think가 와야 합니다.
det.analysis: 원문: ... better impressions than they think.
det.tip: 어법 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: Have you ever asked yourself (A) <u>[whether / that]</u> you made a good impression on someone you just met? In fact, most people believe they make a worse impression than they actually do. The researchers coined a new term, the "liking gap," for this difference in perception or the mismatch between how we perceive ourselves and (B) <u>[what / that]</u> others actually think of us. Our fixed attitudes may prevent us from (C) <u>[reaching / to reach]</u> our true potential.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: [원문/해석] (A) asked yourself whether you made a good impression → 좋은 인상을 주었는지(여부) 물어본 적 있나요? whether(~인지 아닌지). (B) what others actually think of us → 타인이 실제로 우리를 어떻게 생각하는지. think of 뒤 목적어 필요 → what. (C) prevent us from reaching → 도달하는 것을 막다. prevent from + v-ing.
det.analysis:
✅ ① whether – what – reaching
❌ ② whether – that – to reach
❌ ③ that – what – reaching
❌ ④ that – that – to reach
❌ ⑤ whether – what – to reach
det.tip: 어법 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: I wasn't a musical genius, but I was better than most. I was popular at school festivals, and I thought I <u>ⓐ was born</u> to be a musician. In college, I had to compete with classmates <u>ⓑ who</u> were definitely more capable than I was. I kept <u>ⓒ failing</u> no matter how hard I tried. It seemed like every disappointment <u>ⓓ making</u> me lose hope more and more.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: 매번 실망할 때마다 점점 더 희망을 잃게 만드는 것 같았습니다. It seemed like 뒤에 절(S+V)이 와야 하므로 making(현재분사)이 아니라 made(과거 동사)가 와야 합니다.
det.analysis: 원문: It seemed like every disappointment made me lose hope more and more.
det.tip: 어법 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: We often (A) <u>[underestimate / overestimate]</u> ourselves based on our assumption of how others might judge us. In other words, our fixed attitudes may prevent us from reaching our true potential. Don't worry about the impression you think you make on people; chances are you can be (B) <u>[confident / doubtful]</u> that the impression you make is just fine. Many people believe that their personality falls into a specific category and often (C) <u>[blame / praise]</u> their weaknesses or failures on their personality type.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: (A) 우리는 흔히 우리 자신을 과소평가합니다 → underestimate. (B) 여러분이 주는 인상은 괜찮다고 확신해도 된다 → confident. (C) 약점이나 실패를 성격 유형 탓으로 돌린다 → blame.
det.analysis:
✅ ① underestimate – confident – blame
❌ ② overestimate – confident – praise
❌ ③ underestimate – doubtful – blame
❌ ④ overestimate – doubtful – blame
❌ ⑤ underestimate – confident – praise
det.tip: 어휘 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: The researchers coined a new term, the "liking gap," for this difference in perception or the ① <u>mismatch</u> between how we perceive ourselves and what others actually think of us. We often ② <u>underestimate</u> ourselves based on our assumption of how others might judge us. In other words, our ③ <u>flexible</u> attitudes may prevent us from reaching our true potential. Personality categorizations are neither ④ <u>absolute</u> nor ⑤ <u>permanent</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: 우리의 고정된 태도는 우리가 진정한 잠재력에 도달하는 것을 막을 수 있습니다. ③ flexible(유연한)은 원문의 fixed(고정된)와 반대 의미입니다.
det.analysis: 원문: our fixed attitudes may prevent us from reaching our true potential
det.tip: 어휘 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: Last year, after 20 years of hard work, I finally signed my first record company contract. My grandfather was a classical guitarist, and on my 13th birthday, he gave me this picture and a new guitar. After he passed away, I hung it up in my room as a ① <u>reminder</u> of his love for music. I wasn't a musical genius, but I was better than most. I was ② <u>popular</u> at school festivals, and I thought I was born to be a musician. But things were far from ③ <u>easy</u>. In college, I had to ④ <u>cooperate</u> with classmates who were definitely more capable than I was. I don't even remember how many contests I went to and came up ⑤ <u>short</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: 저는 저보다 더 능력 있는 동급생들과 경쟁해야 했습니다. ④ cooperate(협력하다)는 원문의 compete(경쟁하다)와 반대 의미입니다.
det.analysis: 원문: I had to compete with classmates who were definitely more capable than I was.
det.tip: 어휘 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: Most people believe they make a worse impression than they actually do. Researchers performed an experiment where students were paired up for five-minute ice breaking conversations. Most participants' estimations of their partners' responses were pessimistic, which were opposite to the real responses. The researchers coined a new term, the "liking gap," for this difference in perception. We often underestimate ourselves based on our assumption of how others might judge us. Don't worry about the impression you think you make on people; chances are you can be confident that the impression you make is just fine.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: 사람들은 실제보다 나쁜 인상을 준다고 믿지만, 실험 결과 참가자들의 추정은 비관적이었고 실제와 반대였습니다. 연구자들은 이를 호감 격차(liking gap)라고 명명했습니다. 핵심 주제: 타인에게 주는 인상을 과소평가하는 경향.
det.analysis:
❌ ① the importance of making good first impressions
✅ ② the tendency to underestimate the impression we make on others
❌ ③ how to improve social skills in ice breaking conversations
❌ ④ the relationship between pessimism and social anxiety
❌ ⑤ the need for more psychological experiments on perception
det.tip: 대의 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

the tendency to underestimate the impression we make on others
how to improve social skills in ice breaking conversations

questions.passage: The second point I want to make today is about thinking that your personality is fixed. Many people believe that their personality falls into a specific category and often blame their weaknesses or failures on their personality type. However, personality categorizations are neither absolute nor permanent. Try to remember yourself from ten years ago. Just like your likes and future dreams keep changing, so do you. If you choose to behave differently and make needed changes, your personality will also change. People are predictable and consistent over time only because they choose to be, so don't limit yourself to a certain type.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: 성격이 고정되어 있다는 생각에 대한 이야기. 성격 분류는 절대적이지도 영구적이지도 않으며, 다르게 행동하면 성격도 바뀝니다. 핵심: 성격은 생각만큼 고정적이지 않다!
det.analysis:
✅ ① Your Personality: Not as Fixed as You Think
❌ ② How to Find Your True Personality Type
❌ ③ Why People Fear Change in Their Lives
❌ ④ The Science Behind Personality Testing
❌ ⑤ Accepting Who You Are Without Change
det.tip: 대의 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

ch: Your Personality: Not as Fixed as You Think
How to Find Your True Personality Type
Why People Fear Change in Their Lives
Accepting Who You Are Without Change

det.korean: 피카소도 극히 일부만 인정받았고, 할아버지는 명성 없이도 평생 연주를 사랑했습니다. 계속 연주해야 한다는 깨달음. 수많은 프로듀서에게 보낸 끝에 성공. 기회는 준비된 자에게만 온다.

questions.passage: The researchers coined a new term, the "liking gap," for this difference in perception or the mismatch between how we perceive ourselves and what others actually think of us. How is this helpful for you? We often underestimate ourselves based on our assumption of how others might judge us.
questions.stem:
다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸에 들어갈 단어를 주어진 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.

[조건] 본문에서 사용된 단어를 그대로 사용할 것

The researchers coined a new term, the "________," for the mismatch between how we perceive ourselves and what others actually think of us.

det.korean: 연구자들은 호감 격차(liking gap)라는 새로운 용어를 만들었습니다.
det.analysis: 원문: The researchers coined a new term, the "liking gap"
det.tip: 서술형 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: We often underestimate ourselves based on our assumption of how others might judge us. In other words, our fixed attitudes may prevent us from reaching our true potential. Don't worry about the impression you think you make on people.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 주어진 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.

[조건] ① 5단어로 쓸 것 ② prevent, from을 반드시 포함할 것

우리의 고정된 태도는 우리가 진정한 잠재력에 도달하는 것을 막을 수 있습니다.
→ Our fixed attitudes may __________ our true potential.

det.korean: 우리의 고정된 태도는 우리가 진정한 잠재력에 도달하는 것을 막을 수 있습니다.
det.analysis: 원문: Our fixed attitudes may prevent us from reaching our true potential.
det.tip: 서술형 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: If you choose to behave differently and make needed changes, your personality will also change. People are predictable and consistent over time only because they choose to be, so don't limit yourself to a certain type. Start crafting the person you want to become today.
questions.stem:
다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오.

People are predictable and consistent over time only because they choose (be) __________.

det.korean: 그들이 그렇게 되기로 선택했기 때문에. choose + to-v 구문에서 to be는 대부정사.
det.analysis: 원문: they choose to be
det.tip: 서술형 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.
